# rework r6 claims — purchases_returns_and_price_adjustments

- Item 1 (registry credit shortfall: registrant courtesy read a binding owned by the held-funds rate factor) → The selection of the registry holding the spent credit is now a plain, non-factor binding. The rule states it once ("the registry holding the spent credit"), and its basis quotes that phrase. The held-funds rate factor now owns only the registry status, the active-card read and the rate. The registrant courtesy factor reads the registry's bonus parameter through the shared selection, not through a binding another factor owns. Rule wording, ladders, baselines and figures are unchanged.
- Item 2 (note shortfall: the linked service rate when the number was captured but no active membership exists) → The linked tier of the compute now also requires an active Finch Circle membership, read on its own, as the rule says ("whose active membership was enrolled fewer than the veteran months"). A captured number with no active membership now takes the standard rate in both the rule and the compute. The veteran tier already needed an active membership, because the enrolled months are zero without one.
- Item 3 (duplicate capture: the bank-fee allowance did not check for a second capture) → Both allowance tiers now apply only when the unit carries more than one capture of the latest capture's tender. That count is a non-factor binding the policy already read for the refunded capture.
  - The rule's last fee tier now reads "every other case, including a unit with no second capture".
  - The same single-capture gap in the held-capture day count was closed: the debit/cash and bank-card day methods also require a second capture, and the rule's last day tier now reads "in every other case, including a unit with no second capture".
  - Ladders, bases and baselines carry the same text.
- Item 4 (shelf-price correction description claimed a price change on the order) → The description now says that the corrected price is recorded only on the new price adjustment entry and that the selling price on the purchase record is left as rung. The argument description says the same. The name, signature and body are unchanged.
  - The same class in the registry price protection claim was fixed. Its description said the lower price became "the unit's new price"; it now says the lower price is recorded as the new unit price on the entry and the purchase's selling price is left as charged.
  - One prerequisite-effect sentence in the extended charter was reworded the same way.
- R5-O1 (stale store discount wording in task 1's test rationale) → The sentence now says the note paid part of the selling price, so the tax on the note's part is uncorrected. No passage of task 1 calls a Finch Note a store discount.
- Class sweep, factor dependencies → For every factor of all seven policies, the bindings its tiers read were listed transitively and checked mechanically against the bindings other factors own. After item 1, no factor reads a binding owned by another factor in any policy.
- Class sweep, tier scope versus compute → Every tier sentence of all seven rules was compared with its compute branch for the absent-record and single-record cases:
  - no active membership;
  - no active card;
  - no registry credit or registry gift;
  - no expired note;
  - a single payment capture;
  - no gift card redemption;
  - no corrections.

  Apart from items 2 and 3, every branch already takes the tier the rule names. The price protection claim's lower price exists whenever its eligibility holds.
- Class sweep, descriptions versus bodies → Every effect stated in every tool description was checked against its body. Each tool creates one adjustment entry, records the refund tender from the purchase, and lowers the purchase's amount paid and not refunded. The statements that a note, registry credit, card balance or payment entry is left unchanged match bodies that do not touch them. Only the two price statements in item 4 overreached.
- Probes → On scratch copies:
  - a captured number with every membership closed takes the standard note service rate;
  - a unit with its later capture removed takes the standard bank-fee allowance and the whole-weeks day count, with no refunded capture.
- Scored values → None moved in either task. Task 0's world, text and figures are unchanged. Task 1's world and figures are unchanged; only its rationale was edited, and a rework log entry was appended.
